items.title: 67259_Big Chief Moore oral history interview
items.q: I used to go to an old man by the name of Skomuck on the reservation... we'd go over and listen to him sing the chants of the Pimas.

ctx.x: Could you tell us something of your early life and childhood there, your earliest involvement -- leading to your earliest involvement in music.

Yes. The best of my recollection, I've always been musical ever since first awakenings about when I was about six years old when I used to go to an old man by the name of Skomuck on the reservation. He was in his ninties,

and a bunch of us kids would bring different gifts like maybe a sack of beans, corn, tobacco, and we'd go over and listen to him sing the chants of the Pimas. And we would listen to the stories of the early days of Pima land in early years when they used to -- the tribe used to fight with the Apaches, and the Pimas would fight with the Apaches and the constant turmoil there in the old days.
